steps.instruction: Rename the `done: boolean` field of the `Todo` interface to `completed: boolean`. Nothing else changes. nextId behaviour stays the same. Update any of your own code or test fixtures that use `done` so they use `completed`.

The Todo type from ./types now has `completed: boolean` in place of `done: boolean`. Update formatTodo/formatList to read `todo.completed` wherever they used `todo.done`. Rendered output must stay exactly the same as before. Update your test fixtures to build Todos with `completed` instead of `done`.

The Todo type from ./types now has `completed: boolean` in place of `done: boolean`. save must write todos to JSON using the `completed` key (not `done`). load must return Todos with `completed`. For backward compatibility, when a loaded item has a legacy boolean `done` key and no `completed` key, map it to `completed` and leave `done` out of the returned object. Any other existing behaviour (e.g. missing file handling) stays the same. Update your test fixtures to use `completed`.

The Todo type from ./types now has `completed: boolean` in place of `done: boolean`. Update add (new todos get `completed: false`), complete (sets `completed: true`), list filtering, and anything else that read or wrote `done` to use `completed`. Keep `ListOptions.includeDone` with its current name and meaning (it now controls whether todos with `completed: true` are included). Output text must stay the same as before. Update your test fixtures to use `completed`.

input.reason: This field rename touches the shared type and every unit that uses it. The Todo interface changes in types, and format, storage and commands are updated to match. Storage writes the new key and still reads files saved with the old "done" key. ListOptions.includeDone keeps its name, since only the Todo field was asked to change.
